newsitem.title: EGYPT: Rain delay for desert art "installation" in Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Rain delay for desert art "installation" in Egypt.

text.p: Rains on the Red Sea coast of Egypt have temporarily doused plans to inaugurate a land art "installation" that the artists say will be the largest in existence.
The three Greek artists had planned to complete the project by November 29 but heavy rains in the last week have flooded the desert plain where they were working.

The installation will be two spirals of 178 cones, half of them above ground and made of sand and the other half incised into the sand of the desert. It will cover 10 hectares (25 acres) near the tourist resort of Hurghada.

"Because of the floods we were out of touch with Hurghada for two days until this morning. Now it looks like it will take a month to get things fixed," Wail Khalid of the Egyptian sponsoring company Orascom said on Wednesday.
"The positives (the cones above ground) are looking good but the negatives are full of water. We tried pumping the water out but we'll have to wait for it to dry out," he told Reuters.

The project is the brainchild of Alexandra Stratou, Danae Stratou and Stella Constantinides, known as the D.A.S.T. Art Team. Once the work is complete, they will document its decay over six months as the wind wears the cones away.
